journey.name: ED-08 A double-tapped Save creates one task, not two
journey.description:
TaskEditorViewModel.onSave returns early when isSaving is already true, and canSave goes false for the duration of the call. Both guards exist for one reason - the save is asynchronous and the button stays on screen while it is in flight - and neither is observable to a unit test that advances a test dispatcher past the call before the second tap can happen.
The latency knob is what makes the window real: at the default 300-800 ms the second tap lands after the screen has already left. At 3000 ms it lands squarely in the middle of the save.
A duplicate row here is data the user did not ask for and cannot tell apart from what they did.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0 --es qa_latency_ms 3000

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Add task"
Immediately tap the "Save" button a second time, before the screen returns to the list
Verify that the app returns to the "Tasks" screen
Verify that exactly one row reading "Buy milk" is on screen
Verify that exactly five elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
